notes: The current baseline for Welsh energy decarbonisation (SI6), and the evidence the new National Energy Strategy will lean on as it replaces the renewable electricity targets.
summary: The Welsh Government published Energy Generation and Use in Wales: first combined report on 18 March 2026 and revised it on 27 August 2026 after a data error. Renewable electricity generation was equivalent to 55 percent of Welsh electricity consumption in 2024, against targets of 70 percent by 2030 and 100 percent by 2035, while demand was projected to rise from 14.5 TWh in 2024 to 23.8 TWh in 2035, so renewable generation would need to triple. About 31,000 heat pumps had been installed (5 percent of the 580,000 target for 2035), renewable capacity reached 4.8 GW and locally owned capacity 0.99 GW against a 1.5 GW target.
title: Energy generation and use in Wales, first combined report: renewables met 55 percent of 2024 electricity use, and generation must triple for the 2035 target
